query: I'm 10 years from retirement. Should I start de-risking now and how aggressively?

recommendations.title: Initiate Retirement Glide Path - Phase 1 Equity Reduction
recommendations.summary: Begin gradual de-risking by reducing equity exposure from 55% to 50% over the next 12 months, shifting to intermediate-term bonds and dividend-focused equities.
recommendations.detailed_rationale: At 55 with a 10-year horizon to retirement, you should initiate a measured glide path rather than aggressive de-risking. Your current 55% equity allocation (40% ETF + 15% stock) is appropriate for early glide-path phase. Given your moderate risk tolerance, stable income, and $1.8M retirement goal, recommend reducing equity by 5% over 12 months to 50%, then continuing gradual 2-3% annual reductions. This preserves growth potential while beginning risk mitigation. With $755K net worth and 10 years to compound, you need approximately 6-7% annualized returns to reach your goal, requiring continued equity exposure. Aggressive de-risking now would jeopardize retirement targets. Your strong income ($220K) and low debt provide cushion to maintain measured approach.
recommendations.suggested_action: Reduce high-growth equity positions by $42,500 (5% of portfolio) and allocate 3% to intermediate-term investment-grade bonds (VGIT/VCIT) and 2% to dividend aristocrat ETFs (VIG/SCHD). Establish annual rebalancing calendar for 2026-2034.

recommendations.title: Add Treasury Inflation-Protected Securities (TIPS) Ladder
recommendations.summary: Allocate 10% of portfolio to TIPS maturing 2029-2034 to hedge inflation risk during pre-retirement accumulation phase and early retirement.
recommendations.detailed_rationale: Your bond allocation (35%) is currently appropriate but lacks inflation protection critical for pre-retirees. With retirement income needs of $80-100K annually, purchasing power erosion is a significant risk. TIPS provide real return guarantee while reducing sequence-of-returns risk in your final working decade. Creating a ladder with maturities aligned to your 60-65 age range provides predictable real income as you transition to retirement. This 10% allocation ($85K) represents measured diversification within your fixed income sleeve without over-concentrating. TIPS currently offer real yields of 2%+, providing inflation-adjusted returns superior to nominal bonds in inflationary environments. This complements your existing BND holding and enhances portfolio resilience.
recommendations.suggested_action: Allocate $85,000 (10% of portfolio) from existing bond holdings into TIPS ETFs or individual TIPS bonds maturing 2029-2034. Consider SCHP for broad exposure or build custom ladder with individual securities through Treasury Direct. Rebalance semi-annually.

recommendations.title: Enhance Dividend Income Stream for Retirement Transition
recommendations.summary: Increase allocation to quality dividend-paying stocks and funds from current levels to 20% of equity portion, targeting 3-4% yield for retirement income bridge.
recommendations.detailed_rationale: Your healthcare and financial sector holdings (JNJ, UNH, JPM, BRK.B) provide some dividend income, but optimizing for reliable, growing dividends becomes increasingly important as retirement approaches. By dedicating 20% of your equity allocation (~$93.5K) to dividend aristocrats and high-quality dividend payers, you create a more predictable income stream that can supplement retirement withdrawals and reduce sequence risk. This strategy maintains equity exposure for growth while shifting toward lower-volatility, income-generating equities. Your advanced investment experience and stable income support this tactical shift. Target companies with 20+ year dividend growth histories, yielding 3-4%, which provides inflation-hedged income superior to bonds while maintaining equity upside. This bridges accumulation and decumulation phases.
recommendations.suggested_action: Reallocate $50,000 from growth-oriented equity positions (primarily from VTI) into dividend-focused ETFs. Target allocation: 10% to SCHD (US dividend aristocrats), 5% to VIG (dividend growth), 5% to international dividend payers (VIGI). Monitor quarterly for dividend sustainability and growth rates >5% annually.

recommendations.title: Maintain Core Healthcare and Quality Holdings
recommendations.summary: Retain JNJ, UNH, JPM, BRK.B, and PG as portfolio anchors providing defensive characteristics, dividends, and quality factor exposure appropriate for pre-retirement phase.
recommendations.detailed_rationale: Your individual stock selections demonstrate strong quality bias appropriate for transitioning to retirement. JNJ and PG provide defensive consumer staples/healthcare exposure with reliable dividends. UNH offers healthcare growth with secular tailwinds. JPM and BRK.B deliver financial sector diversification with capital discipline and shareholder-friendly management. These holdings (representing 15% of portfolio) provide sector balance, lower volatility than broad market, and proven track records through market cycles. At this life stage, avoid the temptation to trade these quality positions. Their combined characteristics - consistent dividend growth, defensive revenue streams, strong balance sheets, and professional management - align perfectly with de-risking objectives while maintaining growth potential. Continue dollar-cost averaging into these positions through dividend reinvestment. Your 22% healthcare allocation is elevated but justified given demographic trends and defensive properties.
recommendations.suggested_action: Maintain current positions with automatic dividend reinvestment enabled. Review quarterly for fundamental deterioration but avoid tactical trading. If individual positions exceed 5% of portfolio due to appreciation, trim to rebalance. No immediate action required.
